articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumped AWS GovCloud keys and internal secrets on public GitHub because apparently cybersecurity agencies love irony. Nothing says 'secure infrastructure' quite like your crown jewels sitting on the internet's front porch.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress finally woke up to demand answers after CISA's spectacular self-own went public. When the cybersecurity agency becomes the cybersecurity incident, you know we're living in the timeline where satire writes itself.

articles.title: UK banks offered access to OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 amid exclusion from Anthropic’s Glasswing expansion
articles.summary: Bug hunters are rage-quitting Microsoft's broken disclosure process and just dumping exploits into the wild. When researchers start following Nightmare Eclipse's 'fuck it, we'll do it live' approach, maybe it's time to fix your vulnerability handling, Redmond.

articles.title: In bed with Andrew Sa
articles.summary: Autonomous AI discovered a 2-year-old RCE flaw in Redis that humans somehow missed. The machines are now better at finding ways to break our systems than we are—definitely not ominous at all.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)
articles.summary: Microsoft left a debug flag enabled in production Office apps, letting any Android app steal your account tokens. It's like leaving your house keys in the front door, except the door is connected to your entire digital life.

articles.title: Malicious Notifications Could Trick Google Gemini Users
articles.summary: Another Microsoft authentication bypass because apparently security settings are more like security suggestions in Redmond. Android Office apps were handing out login credentials like Halloween candy.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Social engineers tricked Meta's AI support bot into hijacking Obama's old Instagram account for some pro-Iranian redecoration. When artificial intelligence meets artificial intelligence, chaos ensues.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philly cops are surveilling citizens who dare criticize AI data centers because apparently the First Amendment doesn't apply to tech criticism. Nothing says 'land of the free' like monitoring people for having opinions about algorithms.

articles.title: Tropical Blend: Cyber & Politics Ramp Up Across Latin America
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints because mission creep is a feature, not a bug. Your daily commute is now a comprehensive government surveillance log.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle WebLogic flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Oracle WebLogic's CVE-2024-21182 just hit CISA's KEV catalog after active exploitation in the wild. Another day, another enterprise Java disaster that probably should have been patched when the pyramids were still under construction.
